region: Holy Roman Empire, Low Countries, Switzerland and Italy (1400–1806; German and Italian states to 1871/1861)

polities.name: Holy Roman Empire
polities.note: Umbrella polity only: German-kingdom core outline c.1500 (imperial Italy and Low Countries after 1648 excluded). Constituent territories are listed separately and should be drawn on top. Seat = usual imperial residence; Imperial Diet at Regensburg from 1663.

polities.name: Electorate of Mainz
polities.note: Extent = Rhine–Main core (Mainz, Rheingau, Aschaffenburg, Odenwald pieces). Large exclaves: Eichsfeld (Heiligenstadt) and Erfurt (effective from 1664). Left bank lost to France 1797; remnant became Aschaffenburg principality 1803.

polities.name: Electorate of Trier
polities.note: Moselle corridor from Trier to Koblenz plus Westerwald pieces. French-occupied 1794, left bank annexed 1797/1801.

polities.name: Electorate of Cologne
polities.note: Extent = Rhenish strip (Oberstift/Niederstift, Rheinberg–Andernach); the free city of Cologne was not part of it. Also held Vest Recklinghausen and the Duchy of Westphalia (listed separately). Seat Bonn (residence from 1597).

polities.name: Duchy of Westphalia (Electoral Cologne)
polities.note: Sauerland territory ruled by the archbishop-electors of Cologne; to Hesse-Darmstadt 1803.

polities.name: Electoral Palatinate
polities.note: Lower (Rhenish) Palatinate. Electoral dignity transferred to Bavaria 1623–1648 (Palatinate occupied by Spain/Bavaria 1621–1648). Personal union with Bavaria from 1777; left bank to France 1797, right bank to Baden 1803. Jülich-Berg held by the electors 1685–1806 (listed separately).

polities.name: Upper Palatinate
polities.note: Northern Palatinate lands governed from Amberg; ceded to Bavaria 1628 (confirmed 1648). Partly held by side-lines (Palatinate-Neumarkt 1410–1448).

polities.name: Electorate of Saxony
polities.note: 1356–1423 Ascanian Saxe-Wittenberg only; 1423 to the Wettins (Meissen+Thuringia). Leipzig partition 1485: Ernestines kept the electorate (Wittenberg, much of Thuringia) until 1547; Albertines (Dresden) held it 1547–1806 and gained the Lusatias 1635. Became Kingdom of Saxony 1806.

polities.name: Duchy of Saxony (Albertine)
polities.note: Albertine share of the 1485 Leipzig partition (Meissen, Leipzig, northern Thuringia pieces); gained the electorate 1547.

polities.name: Kingdom of Saxony
polities.note: Lost northern half (Wittenberg, Lower Lusatia, eastern Upper Lusatia) to Prussia 1815. Member of the German Confederation, then North German Confederation 1866, German Empire 1871.

polities.name: Margraviate of Brandenburg
polities.note: Hohenzollern from 1415. Neumark held by the Teutonic Order 1402–1455. From 1618 joined with Duchy of Prussia (Brandenburg-Prussia); the margraviate remained the core province of the Kingdom of Prussia. Extent excludes later gains (Farther Pomerania 1653, Magdeburg 1680, Cleves/Mark 1614 etc.).

polities.name: Kingdom of Prussia
polities.note: Extents are the contiguous eastern block only (Brandenburg, Pomerania, East Prussia; Silesia from 1742; West Prussia 1772; Saxon province 1815). Western provinces (Cleves, Mark, Minden, Ravensberg, East Frisia 1744; Rhine Province and Westphalia 1815) are separate blocks—see their own entries. 1701–1742 and 1772 polygons are coarse because East Prussia was not contiguous before 1772 (gap across Royal Prussia).

polities.name: Duchy of Prussia
polities.note: Secularised Teutonic State; personal union with Brandenburg from 1618; sovereign 1657 (Treaty of Wehlau); kingdom 1701. Outside the Empire.

polities.name: State of the Teutonic Order
polities.note: Before 1466 also Pomerelia (Danzig) and Kulmerland; Neumark 1402–1455; Livonian branch separate. Second Peace of Thorn 1466 ceded Royal Prussia to Poland.

polities.name: Teutonic Order (Mergentheim)
polities.note: After 1525 the Grand Master ruled the Order's scattered HRE bailiwicks from Mergentheim (Franconia); other commanderies at Altshausen (Alsace-Burgundy bailiwick), Koblenz, Ellingen. Annexed by Württemberg 1809.

polities.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
polities.note: Extent = Bohemia proper. Crown lands Moravia, Silesia and the Lusatias listed separately. Hussite period 1419–1436 with fragmented control; Habsburg from 1526; elector of the Empire.

polities.name: Margraviate of Moravia
polities.note: Bohemian crown land; held by Hungary (Matthias Corvinus) 1469–1490.

polities.name: Silesian duchies (Bohemian Silesia)
polities.note: Patchwork of Piast duchies (Legnica-Brieg, Oels, Opole-Racibórz, Teschen, Glogau, etc.) under the Bohemian crown; Piast lines died out progressively (last 1675). Conquered by Prussia 1740–1742 except Austrian Silesia (Troppau/Teschen).

polities.name: Upper Lusatia
polities.note: Estates-governed land dominated by the Lusatian League of Six Towns (Bautzen, Görlitz, Zittau, Lauban, Kamenz, Löbau). Ceded to Saxony 1635 (Peace of Prague); eastern half to Prussia 1815.

polities.name: Lower Lusatia
polities.note: Cottbus enclave belonged to Brandenburg from 1462. To Saxony 1635, to Prussia 1815.

polities.name: Archduchy of Austria
aliases: Austria below and above the Enns
polities.note: Austria below the Enns (Vienna) and above the Enns (Linz). Duchy until 1453 (Albertine line until 1457). Vienna occupied by Matthias Corvinus of Hungary 1485–1490. Innviertel added 1779. Core of the Habsburg Monarchy; Austrian Empire from 1804.

polities.name: Inner Austria
polities.note: Duchies of Styria, Carinthia and Carniola (+ Gorizia from 1500, Trieste). Separately ruled by the Leopoldian line 1379–1457 and Archduke Charles II's line 1564–1619; otherwise directly under the Habsburg head.

polities.name: County of Tyrol
polities.note: Habsburg since 1363. Ruled by separate Habsburg lines 1406–1490 and 1564–1665 (with Further Austria). Prince-bishoprics of Trent and Brixen are enclaved (listed separately). Bavarian 1805–1814.

polities.name: Further Austria
polities.note: Scattered Habsburg lands west of Tyrol: Sundgau/Upper Alsace (to France 1648), Breisgau, Forest Towns, Swabian Austria (Burgau, Hohenberg, Nellenburg), Vorarlberg. Extent shows only the Upper Rhine core. Breisgau to Baden 1805.

polities.name: Principality of Lüneburg
polities.note: Welf principality on the Lüneburg Heath; seat Celle from 1371. Inherited by the Elector of Hanover 1705.

polities.name: Principality of Calenberg
polities.note: Gained Göttingen 1495 and Grubenhagen 1665; raised to the Electorate of Hanover 1692.

polities.name: Principality of Göttingen
polities.note: Southern Welf principality around Göttingen, Münden, Northeim; merged into Calenberg 1495.

polities.name: Principality of Grubenhagen
polities.note: Small Welf principality (Einbeck, Osterode, Herzberg) on the western Harz; to Wolfenbüttel 1596, to Calenberg 1617/1665.

polities.name: Principality of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel
polities.note: City of Brunswick largely self-governing until subdued 1671. Part of Kingdom of Westphalia 1807–1813; restored as Duchy of Brunswick 1815–1918 (same core).

polities.name: Duchy of Brunswick
polities.note: Successor of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel; several exclaves (Blankenburg, Holzminden area).

polities.name: Electorate of Hanover
polities.note: Calenberg + Grubenhagen + Göttingen; Lüneburg 1705; Bremen-Verden 1715/1719; Saxe-Lauenburg 1689/1705. French/Prussian occupation 1803–1813; partly in Kingdom of Westphalia 1810–13.

polities.name: Kingdom of Hanover
polities.note: Added Hildesheim, East Frisia, Osnabrück, Lingen, Meppen 1815. The polygon envelope includes the enclaved Grand Duchy of Oldenburg and city of Bremen—draw those on top. Annexed by Prussia 1866.

polities.name: Prince-Archbishopric of Bremen
polities.note: Elbe–Weser triangle; the city of Bremen was de facto independent. Lutheran administrators from 1566. Secularised to Sweden 1648 (Bremen-Verden).

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Verden
polities.note: Small territory around Rotenburg and Verden; secularised to Sweden 1648.

polities.name: Bremen-Verden (Swedish)
polities.note: Duchies of Bremen and Verden under the Swedish crown; occupied by Denmark 1712, sold to Hanover 1715 (confirmed 1719).

polities.name: Bavaria-Munich
polities.note: Wittelsbach partition duchy of Upper Bavaria; absorbed Ingolstadt share 1447 (via Landshut, partly) and Landshut 1505 after the War of the Succession of Landshut, reuniting Bavaria.

polities.name: Bavaria-Landshut
polities.note: Lower Bavaria with Burghausen; took Ingolstadt 1447 and half of Straubing 1429. Line extinct 1503; War of Landshut Succession 1503–05.

polities.name: Bavaria-Ingolstadt
polities.note: Scattered duchy (Ingolstadt, Wasserburg, Kufstein, Kitzbühel, Rattenberg, parts of Upper Bavaria). To Bavaria-Landshut 1447.

polities.name: Bavaria-Straubing
polities.note: Wittelsbach duchy of Straubing, in personal union with Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut (to 1433). Partitioned among the other Bavarian dukes 1429.

polities.name: Duchy of Bavaria
polities.note: Reunited 1505; Electorate 1623; Upper Palatinate 1628. Innviertel lost to Austria 1779. Personal union with Palatinate 1777. Kingdom 1806. Austrian occupation 1704–1714 and 1742–1745.

polities.name: Kingdom of Bavaria
polities.note: 1806–1814 included Tyrol, Vorarlberg, Salzburg (1810–16), Ansbach, Bayreuth (1810). From 1816 also the Rhenish Palatinate exclave (Speyer) west of the Rhine, not included in polygon.

polities.name: Württemberg
polities.note: County, partitioned Urach/Stuttgart 1442–1482; duchy 1495; Habsburg-occupied 1520–1534 and Austrian fief 1534–1599. Also held Montbéliard (County of Montbéliard). Electorate 1803; Kingdom 1806 (see Kingdom of Württemberg).

polities.name: Kingdom of Württemberg
polities.note: Doubled in size 1802–1810 (Upper Swabian abbeys, imperial cities, Ulm 1810).

polities.name: Margraviate of Baden
polities.note: Scattered Upper Rhine lands (Baden, Pforzheim, Durlach, Hachberg, Rötteln/Sausenberg from 1503). Partitioned 1535 into Baden-Baden and Baden-Durlach.

polities.name: Margraviate of Baden-Baden
polities.note: Catholic line; middle Baden plus Sponheim shares on the Moselle. Inherited by Baden-Durlach 1771.

polities.name: Margraviate of Baden-Durlach
polities.note: Protestant line; also the southern Markgräflerland (Hachberg, Rötteln, Badenweiler) not shown in polygon. Reunited Baden 1771.

polities.name: Baden (Margraviate 1771, Grand Duchy 1806)
polities.note: Reunited 1771; electorate 1803; grand duchy 1806 with Breisgau, Palatinate right bank, Constance, Fürstenberg lands.

polities.name: County of Montbéliard
polities.note: Württemberg side-possession west of Basel; annexed by France 1793.

polities.name: Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen
polities.note: Swabian Hohenzollern county, principality 1623; ceded to Prussia 1850.

polities.name: Hohenzollern-Hechingen
polities.note: County, principality 1623; ceded to Prussia 1850.

polities.name: Fürstenberg
polities.note: Baar and Kinzig valley counties (Fürstenberg, Heiligenberg); principality 1664; reunited 1744; mediatised 1806 (to Baden).

polities.name: Hohenlohe counties
polities.note: Several Hohenlohe lines (Neuenstein, Waldenburg; princely from 1744/1764) between Kocher and Tauber; mediatised to Württemberg/Bavaria 1806.

polities.name: Landgraviate of Hesse
polities.note: Lower Hesse (Kassel) + Upper Hesse (Marburg; partitioned 1458–1500); County of Katzenelnbogen inherited 1479. Divided among Philip I's sons 1567.

polities.name: Hesse-Kassel
polities.note: Gained half of Hesse-Marburg 1604/1648, part of Schaumburg 1647, Hanau-Münzenberg 1736 (southern exclave). Electorate 1803; in Kingdom of Westphalia 1807–1813; restored 1814; annexed by Prussia 1866.

polities.name: Hesse-Darmstadt
polities.note: Upper Hesse (Giessen) + Darmstadt/Upper Katzenelnbogen; Grand Duchy 1806 (held Duchy of Westphalia 1803–1816); Rhenish Hesse (Mainz, Worms) from 1816.

polities.name: Hesse-Marburg
polities.note: Partitioned between Hesse-Kassel and Hesse-Darmstadt 1604 (dispute to 1648).

polities.name: Hesse-Homburg
polities.note: Cadet landgraviate; sovereign 1815 with Meisenheim exclave; to Hesse-Darmstadt then Prussia 1866.

polities.name: County of Katzenelnbogen
polities.note: Lower County on the Middle Rhine (St. Goar) and Upper County around Darmstadt; inherited by Hesse 1479.

polities.name: County of Hanau
polities.note: Hanau-Münzenberg (Kinzig valley, Hanau) to Hesse-Kassel 1736; Hanau-Lichtenberg (northern Alsace, seat Bouxwiller 48.83,7.48, from 1480) to Hesse-Darmstadt 1736.

polities.name: Nassau-Dillenburg
polities.note: Ottonian Nassau lands (Dillenburg, Siegen, Dietz, Hadamar); line of the princes of Orange. Divided among sub-lines 1606; reunited under Nassau-Dietz 1739/1743 (Orange-Nassau), French/Berg 1806, Prussia 1815.

polities.name: Nassau-Weilburg
polities.note: Walramian line on the Lahn and Taunus; merged with Nassau-Usingen into the Duchy of Nassau 1806/1816.

polities.name: Nassau-Saarbrücken
polities.note: Saar county held by Walramian Nassau; annexed by France 1797.

polities.name: Nassau-Usingen
polities.note: Walramian line; principality 1688; merged into Duchy of Nassau.

polities.name: Duchy of Nassau
polities.note: Union of Nassau-Usingen and Nassau-Weilburg; seat Weilburg/Biebrich then Wiesbaden; annexed by Prussia 1866.

polities.name: Palatinate-Neuburg
polities.note: Created 1505 for the Palatine heirs of Bavaria-Landshut. Gained Jülich-Berg 1614 (ruled from Düsseldorf); inherited the Electorate 1685; merged into Palatinate-Sulzbach inheritance 1742.

polities.name: Palatinate-Zweibrücken
polities.note: Western Palatine duchy (Zweibrücken, Veldenz, Meisenheim, Bischweiler). Kings of Sweden were dukes 1654–1718. Annexed by France 1797; its dukes inherited Bavaria 1799.

polities.name: Palatinate-Simmern
polities.note: Hunsrück duchy with shares of Sponheim; its line inherited the Electorate 1559; lands reabsorbed 1598 (later a second Simmern line to 1673).

polities.name: Palatinate-Mosbach
polities.note: Odenwald/Neckar duchy (with Neumarkt from 1448); reverted to the Electorate 1499.

polities.name: Palatinate-Sulzbach
polities.note: Small Upper Palatinate duchy; its duke Charles Theodore became Elector Palatine 1742 and Elector of Bavaria 1777.

polities.name: Principality of Ansbach
polities.note: Franconian Hohenzollern margraviate (Onolzbach); united with Bayreuth 1769; sold to Prussia 1791; to Bavaria 1806.

polities.name: Principality of Bayreuth
polities.note: Margraviate of Brandenburg-Kulmbach; seat moved to Bayreuth 1604; Prussian 1791; to Bavaria 1810.

polities.name: County of Henneberg
polities.note: Southern Thuringian/Franconian county; extinct 1583, divided between Ernestine and Albertine Saxony (administered jointly until 1660).

polities.name: Duchy of Mecklenburg
polities.note: Duchy from 1348; absorbed Werle 1436 and Stargard 1471. Rostock and Wismar largely autonomous Hanseatic towns. Joint rule/partitions; formally divided 1621.

polities.name: Lordship of Werle
polities.note: Eastern-central Mecklenburg lordship; inherited by Mecklenburg 1436.

polities.name: Mecklenburg-Stargard
polities.note: Duchy of the junior Mecklenburg line (Lordship of Stargard); reverted to Mecklenburg 1471.

polities.name: Mecklenburg-Güstrow
polities.note: Eastern half of Mecklenburg; Wallenstein held both duchies 1628–1631. Line extinct 1695; partition 1701 created Mecklenburg-Strelitz.

polities.name: Mecklenburg-Schwerin
polities.note: Western half 1621–1695; all Mecklenburg except Strelitz after 1701. Wismar Swedish 1648–1803. Grand duchy 1815.

polities.name: Mecklenburg-Strelitz
polities.note: Former Stargard lordship plus the Principality of Ratzeburg exclave (west, near Lübeck). Grand duchy 1815.

polities.name: Pomerania-Wolgast
polities.note: Hither Pomerania and Rügen (Barth, Stralsund, Greifswald, Wolgast). Merged in united Pomerania 1478–1532; re-partitioned 1532; reunited 1625 under Bogislaw XIV. Gap 1478–1532 (see Duchy of Pomerania).

polities.name: Pomerania-Stettin
polities.note: 1400–1464 small Stettin duchy; extinct 1464 (succession war with Brandenburg). 1532–1625 the Stettin share = Farther Pomerania + Stettin. Gap 1464–1532.

polities.name: Pomerania-Stolp
polities.note: Eastern (Farther) Pomeranian duchy; ruled by Eric of Pomerania (king of Denmark, Sweden, Norway) after 1449; to Wolgast line 1459.

polities.name: Duchy of Pomerania
polities.note: Reunited under Bogislaw X 1478–1532 and Bogislaw XIV 1625–1637 (Swedish-occupied from 1630). Divided 1648/1653: west to Sweden, Farther Pomerania to Brandenburg.

polities.name: Swedish Pomerania
polities.note: Hither Pomerania under Sweden (formalised 1648); Stettin and land south of the Peene lost to Prussia 1720. Danish 1715–1720; French 1807–1810. To Prussia 1815.

polities.name: Holstein
polities.note: Schauenburg county (Holstein-Rendsburg) until 1459; Danish kings elected dukes 1460, duchy 1474. Divided into royal (Glückstadt) and ducal Gottorp shares 1544–1773. Free city of Lübeck, Hamburg excluded. To Prussia/Austria 1864, Prussia 1866.

polities.name: Holstein-Gottorp
polities.note: Ducal share of Schleswig and Holstein (Kiel, Eiderstedt, Gottorf, scattered districts) interleaved with the royal Danish share; Gottorp Schleswig lands seized by Denmark 1713/1721; Holstein share exchanged 1773.

polities.name: Holstein-Pinneberg
polities.note: Schauenburg county northwest of Hamburg; held together with the County of Schaumburg; divided 1640 (Pinneberg to Denmark, Altona).

polities.name: Saxe-Lauenburg

overlord.name: Principality of Lüneburg / Electorate of Hanover

polities.note: Ascanian duchy (with Land Hadeln exclave at the Elbe mouth). Line extinct 1689; to Lüneburg/Hanover; Denmark 1815; Prussia 1865.

polities.name: County of Oldenburg
polities.note: Oldenburg and Delmenhorst; Jever added 1575–1667; Butjadingen conquered 1514. Danish 1667–1773; exchanged to Holstein-Gottorp and made a duchy 1774.

polities.name: Duchy of Oldenburg
polities.note: Gained Vechta and Cloppenburg (Oldenburg Münsterland) 1803, Jever 1818; exclaves: Principality of Lübeck (Eutin) and Birkenfeld (1817). Grand duchy 1815/1829.

polities.name: County of East Frisia
polities.note: Cirksena counts (princes from 1654/1662). Emden a near-autonomous city under Dutch protection from 1595. Before 1464 chieftaincies (hovetlinge). To Prussia 1744, Holland 1807, Hanover 1815.

polities.name: Lordship of Jever
polities.note: Frisian chieftain lordship; after Maria of Jever (d.1575) passed to Oldenburg, Anhalt-Zerbst, Russia; Oldenburg 1818.

polities.name: Duchy of Jülich
polities.note: Between Aachen, Cologne and the Meuse. Jülich succession war 1609–1614; Treaty of Xanten 1614 gave Jülich-Berg to Palatinate-Neuburg. French 1794.

polities.name: Duchy of Berg
polities.note: Right bank of the Rhine east of Cologne; became the core of the Grand Duchy of Berg 1806.

polities.name: Duchy of Cleves
polities.note: Lower Rhine duchy (Wesel, Emmerich, Kleve); with the County of Mark from 1398. Brandenburg 1614/1666; west bank to France 1795.

polities.name: County of Mark
polities.note: Ruhr–Sauerland county (Hamm, Unna, Iserlohn); excludes Dortmund. Brandenburg 1614; Grand Duchy of Berg 1808.

polities.name: United Duchies of Jülich-Cleves-Berg
polities.note: Personal union of Jülich, Cleves, Berg, Mark and Ravensberg (Ravensberg detached, near Bielefeld). Polygon is an envelope over non-contiguous parts that encloses Electoral Cologne and Cologne city—draw those above. Extinct 1609 → War of the Jülich Succession.

polities.name: County of Ravensberg
polities.note: Small county around Bielefeld; Brandenburg 1614.

polities.name: Grand Duchy of Berg
polities.note: Napoleonic client state under Joachim Murat then Napoleon's nephew; included Berg, Mark, Münster (east), Dortmund.

polities.name: County of Bentheim
polities.note: County in the Ems/Vechte lands; pledged to Hanover 1753–1803; mediatised 1806.

polities.name: County of Lingen
polities.note: Emsland county; Orange possession then Prussian 1702.

polities.name: County of Tecklenburg
polities.note: Small Westphalian county; sold to Prussia 1707.

polities.name: County of Lippe
polities.note: Lordship, county 1528, principality 1789; seat Detmold from 1613.

polities.name: County of Schaumburg
polities.note: Weser county (Schauenburg); partitioned 1647 between Hesse-Kassel, Lippe (Schaumburg-Lippe) and Brunswick-Lüneburg.

polities.name: Schaumburg-Lippe
polities.note: Western part of old Schaumburg; principality 1807.

polities.name: County of Waldeck
polities.note: County, principality 1712; Pyrmont exclave from 1625.

polities.name: Ernestine Duchy of Saxony
polities.note: Thuringian remnant left to the Ernestines after Mühlberg 1547; jointly ruled then split 1572 into Saxe-Weimar and Saxe-Coburg-Eisenach. All later Ernestine duchies are subdivisions of this area.

polities.name: Saxe-Weimar
polities.note: Repeatedly subdivided (Altenburg 1603, Gotha 1640, Eisenach). United with Eisenach 1741 (Eisenach exclave west); grand duchy 1815 with Neustadt circle. Polygon = Weimar–Jena core.

polities.name: Saxe-Coburg (1572–1638)
polities.note: Coburg duchy (with Eisenach 1572–1596); line extinct 1633/1638, to Saxe-Altenburg then Gotha.

polities.name: Saxe-Eisenach
polities.note: Two separate creations (1596–1638, 1672–1741); to Saxe-Weimar 1741.

polities.name: Saxe-Gotha(-Altenburg)
polities.note: Ernest the Pious's state (Gotha 1640, Altenburg 1672); largest Ernestine duchy c.1672–1680 then partitioned among 7 sons (Meiningen, Hildburghausen, Coburg-Saalfeld etc.). Gotha–Altenburg line extinct 1825.

polities.name: Saxe-Altenburg
polities.note: First creation 1603–1672 (to Gotha); recreated 1826 for the former Hildburghausen line.

polities.name: Saxe-Meiningen
polities.note: Werra valley duchy; enlarged 1826 with Hildburghausen and Saalfeld.

polities.name: Saxe-Hildburghausen
polities.note: Moved to Altenburg 1826.

polities.name: Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld
polities.note: Coburg plus Saalfeld exclave (north); became Saxe-Coburg and Gotha 1826.

polities.name: Saxe-Coburg and Gotha
polities.note: Two non-contiguous parts: Coburg (polygon) and Gotha (50.95,10.70, ~25 km).

polities.name: Saxe-Weissenfels
polities.note: Albertine secundogeniture (Weissenfels, Querfurt); reverted 1746.

polities.name: Saxe-Merseburg
polities.note: Albertine secundogeniture (Merseburg, part of Lusatia); reverted 1738.

polities.name: Saxe-Zeitz
polities.note: Albertine secundogeniture (Zeitz, Naumburg, Neustadt an der Orla); reverted 1718.

polities.name: Schwarzburg
polities.note: Thuringian counties (Arnstadt, Sondershausen, Rudolstadt, Blankenburg); divided 1599 into Rudolstadt (south) and Sondershausen (north) lines.

polities.name: Schwarzburg-Rudolstadt
polities.note: Upper county around Rudolstadt plus Frankenhausen exclave in north; principality 1710.

polities.name: Schwarzburg-Sondershausen
polities.note: Lower county around Sondershausen plus Arnstadt exclave in south; principality 1697/1710.

polities.name: Reuss Elder Line
polities.note: Vogtland counts; principality 1778.

polities.name: Reuss Younger Line
polities.note: Several sub-lines (Gera, Schleiz, Lobenstein, Ebersdorf) united 1848. Before 1564 the Reuss lordships of Plauen, Greiz and Gera (Vogtland, 'Advocates of Weida').

polities.name: County of Mansfeld
polities.note: Copper-mining county east of the Harz; sequestrated by Saxony and Magdeburg 1570; line extinct 1780.

polities.name: County of Stolberg-Wernigerode
polities.note: Stolberg counts in the Harz (Stolberg 51.57,10.95 and Wernigerode from 1429); under Brandenburg-Prussian suzerainty.

polities.name: Principality of Anhalt
polities.note: Ascanian principality between Elbe, Saale and Harz; normally divided among lines (Zerbst, Dessau, Köthen, Bernburg); united 1570–1603 under Joachim Ernst; divided 1603.

polities.name: Anhalt-Dessau
polities.note: Line from 1396/1474; united Anhalt 1863 (Duchy of Anhalt).

polities.name: Anhalt-Zerbst
polities.note: Also held Jever 1667–1793; partitioned among other lines 1793.

polities.name: Anhalt-Köthen
polities.note: Line extinct 1847; to Dessau.

polities.name: Anhalt-Bernburg
polities.note: Old line extinct 1468; new line 1603–1863 (with Harzgerode/Ballenstedt).

polities.name: Duchy of Anhalt
polities.note: Reunited Anhalt.

polities.name: Duchy of Lorraine
polities.note: Enclaves the Three Bishoprics (Metz, Toul, Verdun). Personal union with Bar from 1431/1480 (phase 2 polygon includes Bar). French occupation 1634–1661 and 1670–1697; to Stanisław 1737; annexed by France 1766.

polities.name: Duchy of Bar
polities.note: Western part (Barrois mouvant) held of France. René of Anjou duke 1430; merged with Lorraine 1480.

polities.name: Three Bishoprics (Metz, Toul, Verdun)
polities.note: French-occupied 1552, annexed 1648 (province of the Three Bishoprics). Before 1552: Free City of Metz (city republic) and the separate prince-bishoprics of Metz (Vic-sur-Seille), Toul and Verdun—small, scattered temporalities.

polities.name: Free City of Metz
polities.note: Patrician city republic with the Pays Messin; occupied by France 1552.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Metz
polities.note: Temporal lands of the bishop (Vic, Sarrebourg, Moyenvic) east of Metz; French protectorate 1552.

polities.name: Décapole
polities.note: League of ten Alsatian imperial cities (Haguenau, Colmar, Wissembourg, Sélestat, Obernai, Kaysersberg, Turckheim, Munster, Rosheim, Mulhouse→Landau). Cities scattered along Alsace (lat 47.75–49.05, lon 7.15–7.95); French suzerainty 1648, annexed 1679.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Münster
polities.note: Largest Westphalian ecclesiastical state: Oberstift (Münsterland) and Niederstift (Emsland, Cloppenburg, Vechta) in the north, linked by a narrow corridor. Often held with Cologne. Partitioned 1802/03 (Prussia, Oldenburg, Arenberg, others).

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Paderborn
polities.note: To Prussia 1802.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Würzburg
polities.note: Lower Franconia along the Main; bishops styled dukes of Franconia. Secularised to Bavaria 1803; Grand Duchy of Würzburg 1805–1814.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Bamberg
polities.note: Upper Franconia; also Carinthian exclaves (Villach, Wolfsberg) until 1759. To Bavaria 1802.

polities.name: Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg
polities.note: Alpine ecclesiastical state (Salzach valley, Pongau, Pinzgau, Lungau); also Rupertiwinkel west of the Salzach. Electorate of Salzburg 1803–05; Austria 1805, Bavaria 1810–16.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Liège
polities.note: Meuse valley from Dinant/Bouillon to the Loon (Limburg) county; Liège Revolution 1789–91; annexed by France 1795.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Osnabrück
polities.note: Alternated Catholic bishops and Protestant Brunswick-Lüneburg princes after 1648. To Hanover 1803.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Hildesheim
polities.note: Lost the 'Great Stift' to the Welfs in the Hildesheim Diocesan Feud (1519–23), keeping only the Little Stift until restitution 1643. To Prussia 1803.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Utrecht
polities.note: Nedersticht (Utrecht) and Oversticht (Overijssel, Drenthe), separated by Guelders' Veluwe. Secularised to Charles V 1528 (Lordships of Utrecht and Overijssel).

polities.name: Archbishopric of Magdeburg
polities.note: Middle Elbe/Saale; city of Magdeburg semi-autonomous. Protestant administrators from 1566; to Brandenburg 1680 as Duchy of Magdeburg.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Halberstadt
polities.note: Secularised to Brandenburg 1648 (Principality of Halberstadt).

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Minden
polities.note: Secularised to Brandenburg 1648 (Principality of Minden).

polities.name: Prince-Abbey of Fulda
polities.note: Imperial abbey, prince-bishopric 1752; to Nassau-Orange 1803, Grand Duchy of Frankfurt 1810.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Trent
polities.note: Under Tyrolean protection; secularised to Austria 1803.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Brixen
polities.note: Eisack valley and Puster valley lands; to Austria 1803.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Passau
polities.note: Small territory north and east of the city (Abteiland); to Bavaria 1803.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Augsburg
polities.note: Scattered between Danube and the Alps along Lech/Iller (Dillingen, Füssen); the city of Augsburg was a free city. To Bavaria 1803.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Eichstätt
polities.note: Altmühl valley; to Bavaria 1802/1805.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Speyer
polities.note: Both banks of the Rhine around Speyer/Bruchsal (residence from 1723; Udenheim/Philippsburg earlier); city of Speyer free. To Baden 1803 (left bank to France 1797).

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Strasbourg

overlord.name: Kingdom of France (sovereignty over Alsatian lands)

polities.note: Upper and Lower Mundat in Alsace plus Ortenau lands east of the Rhine; city of Strasbourg was a free city to 1681.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Basel
polities.note: Jura lands; city of Basel independent and Swiss from 1501. Northern part French (Rauracian Republic) 1792, all French by 1797; to Bern 1815.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Constance
polities.note: Small lands around Meersburg and Reichenau; to Baden 1803.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Lübeck
polities.note: Eutin lands; Protestant administrators from Holstein-Gottorp; secularised 1803 as Principality of Lübeck under Oldenburg.

polities.name: Prince-Bishopric of Freising
polities.note: Small territory around Freising plus Werdenfels and Austrian exclaves; to Bavaria 1802.

polities.name: Cambrésis (Prince-Bishopric of Cambrai)
polities.note: Ecclesiastical principality; French 1477–1482; Habsburg garrison from 1543; annexed by France 1678/79.

polities.name: Abbey of Saint Gall
polities.note: Prince-abbot's territory (Fürstenland) plus Toggenburg (1468); the city of St. Gallen separate; associate of the Confederacy. Ended 1798.

polities.name: Free City of Hamburg
polities.note: Hanseatic city; formally imperial 1618/1768; small rural territory (Vierlande jointly with Lübeck, Ritzebüttel/Cuxhaven exclave at 53.87,8.70). Sovereign 1815; German Empire 1871.

polities.name: Free City of Lübeck
polities.note: Head of the Hanseatic League; territory incl. Travemünde; German Empire 1871 (annexed by Prussia 1937).

polities.name: Free City of Bremen
polities.note: Hanseatic city, imperial city status recognised 1646 (Linz diploma); Bremerhaven acquired 1827.

polities.name: Free Imperial City of Nuremberg
polities.note: Largest city-territory in the Empire after the Landshut war 1504–05 (Lauf, Hersbruck, Altdorf). To Bavaria 1806.

polities.name: Free Imperial City of Ulm
polities.note: Ruled c.780 km² (Geislingen, Albeck, Leipheim) at its height. To Bavaria 1802/03, Württemberg 1810.

polities.name: Free City of Frankfurt

overlord.name: Principality of Regensburg / Grand Duchy of Frankfurt

polities.note: Imperial election and coronation city; seat of the German Confederation Diet 1816–66; annexed by Prussia 1866.

polities.name: Free Imperial City of Augsburg
polities.note: Fugger/Welser banking city with minimal rural territory; to Bavaria 1806.

polities.name: Free City of Strasbourg
polities.note: Imperial city republic with rural bailiwicks (Wasselonne, Illkirch etc.); annexed by France 1681.

polities.name: Free Imperial City of Cologne
polities.note: De facto independent from the archbishop since 1288; formally imperial 1475; French 1794/1797.

polities.name: Free Imperial City of Aachen
polities.note: Coronation city with the Aachener Reich rural district; French 1794/1801.

polities.name: Free Imperial City of Dortmund
polities.note: Imperial city with the County of Dortmund; to Nassau-Orange 1803.

polities.name: Free Imperial City of Regensburg
polities.note: Seat of the Perpetual Imperial Diet 1663–1806; Principality of Regensburg (Dalberg) 1803–1810, then Bavaria.

polities.name: Free Imperial City of Rothenburg
polities.note: Held the Landhege, a rural territory of c.400 km²; to Bavaria 1802.

polities.name: Free Imperial City of Schwäbisch Hall
polities.note: Salt city with a sizable rural territory; to Württemberg 1802.

polities.name: Free Imperial City of Rottweil
polities.note: Swiss associate (Zugewandter Ort) 1463/1519–1632; to Württemberg 1802.

polities.name: Republic of Mulhouse
polities.note: Décapole member to 1515, then Swiss associate; voted to join France 1798.

polities.name: Burgundian State
polities.note: Composite of the Valois dukes: southern block = Duchy and Free County of Burgundy (polygon); northern block = the Netherlands provinces listed separately with this as overlord. Charles the Bold also held Lorraine 1475–77 and Guelders 1473–77. Duchy proper to France 1477; rest to Habsburgs (Mary, Maximilian).

polities.name: Duchy of Burgundy
polities.note: French fief, core of the Burgundian State; annexed by France 1477.

polities.name: Free County of Burgundy
polities.note: Imperial fief; French-occupied 1477–1493; Spanish Habsburg province until conquered by France 1674 (ceded 1678). Besançon a separate imperial city to 1654.

polities.name: Duchy of Brabant
polities.note: Includes Antwerp and Limburg-overmaas lands loosely. Burgundian cadet dukes 1406–1430, then Burgundy. North Brabant (States Brabant) to the Dutch Republic 1648 (phase 2 = southern/Austrian Brabant).

polities.name: County of Flanders
polities.note: French crown fief until 1529 (Treaty of Cambrai). Walloon Flanders (Lille) and western parts to France 1668–1678; Zeelandic Flanders to the Dutch 1648.

polities.name: County of Holland
polities.note: With Zeeland and Hainaut in personal union. Jacqueline of Bavaria ceded to Philip the Good 1433. Leading province of the Dutch Republic from 1581.

polities.name: County of Zeeland
polities.note: Islands of the Scheldt delta; province of the Dutch Republic from 1581.

polities.name: Duchy of Guelders
polities.note: Four quarters (Nijmegen, Arnhem/Veluwe, Zutphen, Roermond/Upper Guelders). Egmond and Charles of Egmond resisted Burgundy/Habsburg; Treaty of Venlo 1543 ceded it to Charles V. Afterwards split: Dutch Guelders (1581) and Spanish Upper Guelders (to Prussia 1713).

polities.name: County of Hainaut
polities.note: Southern part (Valenciennes, Maubeuge) to France 1659/1678.

polities.name: Duchy of Luxembourg
polities.note: Luxembourg dynasty's home duchy; to Burgundy 1443. Thionville area to France 1659; French occupation 1684–1697.

polities.name: Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
polities.note: Western (Walloon) half to Belgium 1839; German Confederation member to 1866.

polities.name: County of Namur
polities.note: Sold to Philip the Good 1421.

polities.name: County of Artois
polities.note: French fief until 1529; French conquest 1640, ceded 1659 (Saint-Omer 1678).

polities.name: Frisia (Lordship of Frisia)
polities.note: Before 1498 'Frisian freedom' with chieftains (Schieringers/Vetkopers) and no single ruler. Province of the Dutch Republic from 1581.

polities.name: City of Groningen and Ommelanden
polities.note: Hanseatic city dominating the Frisian Ommelanden; submitted to Charles V 1536; taken by the Dutch 1594 (province Stad en Lande).

polities.name: Habsburg Netherlands
polities.note: Union of Burgundian provinces under Maximilian, Philip the Handsome and Charles V; Frisia 1524, Utrecht/Overijssel 1528, Groningen 1536, Guelders 1543 completed the Seventeen Provinces (Burgundian Circle 1512, Pragmatic Sanction 1549). Enclaves Liège (separate).

polities.name: Spanish Netherlands
polities.note: Philip II's Netherlands; Dutch Revolt from 1568/1572, northern provinces seceded 1581 (front line fluctuated until 1648). Artois 1659 and Walloon Flanders/Cambrai 1678 lost to France. Liège enclaved.

polities.name: Austrian Netherlands
polities.note: French-occupied 1745–1748; United Belgian States revolt 1790; annexed by France 1795. Liège enclaved (separate).

polities.name: Dutch Republic
aliases: Republic of the Seven United Netherlands
polities.note: Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht, Guelders, Overijssel, Friesland, Groningen (+ Drenthe) and the Generality Lands (States Brabant, Zeelandic Flanders, States Limburg) from 1648. Independence recognised 1648.

polities.name: Batavian Republic
polities.note: French sister republic; became Kingdom of Holland 1806.

polities.name: Kingdom of Holland
polities.note: Louis Bonaparte; gained East Frisia and Jever 1807; annexed into France 1810.

polities.name: United Kingdom of the Netherlands
polities.note: Belgian Revolution 1830 (effective split); Belgium recognised 1839; continued as Kingdom of the Netherlands.

polities.name: Kingdom of Belgium
polities.note: Independent 1830 (recognised 1839).

polities.name: Old Swiss Confederacy
polities.note: Eight cantons by 1400 (Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden, Lucerne, Zurich, Glarus, Zug, Bern) + Fribourg & Solothurn 1481, Basel & Schaffhausen 1501, Appenzell 1513; Aargau 1415, Thurgau 1460, Ticino bailiwicks 1512, Vaud (Bern) 1536 as subject lands. Associates (Three Leagues, Valais, St. Gall, Geneva, Mulhouse, Neuchâtel, Biel) listed separately. Seat: no capital; Diet met mostly at Baden (47.47,8.31).

polities.name: Helvetic Republic
polities.note: Unitary French client state; included the Grisons from 1799; Valais detached 1802.

polities.name: Swiss Confederation (1803–)
polities.note: Mediation Act 1803 (19 cantons); 1815 added Valais, Geneva, Neuchâtel; federal state 1848 with Bern as federal city.

polities.name: Three Leagues
aliases: Free State of the Three Leagues
polities.note: League of God's House (1367), Grey League (1395), League of the Ten Jurisdictions (1436), allied 1471. Ruled Valtellina, Chiavenna and Bormio 1512–1797. Joined Helvetic Republic 1799 (canton of Graubünden 1803).

polities.name: Republic of Valais (Seven Tithes)
polities.note: Upper Valais communes (Zenden) and the Prince-Bishop of Sion; conquered Lower Valais from Savoy 1475 (and Monthey 1536) as a subject land. Helvetic 1798–1802; separate Rhodanic/Valais Republic 1802–1810; French département Simplon 1810–13; Swiss canton 1815.

polities.name: Republic of Geneva
polities.note: Expelled bishop and Savoyard vidomne 1534; Calvinist republic. Annexed by France 1798; Swiss canton 1815.

polities.name: Principality of Neuchâtel
polities.note: Orléans-Longueville princes 1504–1707; Prussian king prince 1707–1806, 1814–1848 (Swiss canton 1815 at the same time); republic 1848.

polities.name: Confederation of the Rhine
polities.note: Umbrella of Napoleon's German client states (Bavaria, Württemberg, Saxony, Westphalia, Baden, Berg, Hesse-Darmstadt etc.). Members listed separately; draw them on top.

polities.name: Kingdom of Westphalia
polities.note: Hesse-Kassel, Brunswick, Prussian lands west of the Elbe, part of Hanover (1810).

polities.name: Grand Duchy of Frankfurt
polities.note: Dalberg's state: Frankfurt, Aschaffenburg, Hanau, Fulda, Wetzlar (scattered).

polities.name: Grand Duchy of Würzburg
polities.note: For Ferdinand III of Tuscany; to Bavaria 1814.

polities.name: North German Confederation
polities.note: Prussian-led federal state north of the Main; became the German Empire 1871.

polities.name: German Empire
polities.note: Coarse envelope; federal states listed separately remained as members (draw on top if desired). Includes Alsace-Lorraine from 1871.

polities.name: Duchy of Savoy

overlord.name: Kingdom of France (occupation of Savoy and most of Piedmont)

polities.note: County until 1416. Held Vaud and Bresse until 1536/1601 (Vaud to Bern 1536, Bresse/Bugey to France 1601; Saluzzo gained 1601). French occupation 1536–1559 (court confined around Vercelli/Nice). Capital moved Chambéry→Turin 1563. Part of Montferrat 1631/1708. King of Sicily 1713–1720, then Sardinia.

polities.name: Kingdom of Sardinia (Savoyard)
polities.note: Mainland polygon (Savoy, Piedmont, Nice; Novara/Tortona 1738, Vigevano 1748). Island of Sardinia also part (see island entry). Mainland annexed by France 1796–1802; court on Sardinia 1799–1814. Genoa added 1815; Lombardy 1859; Savoy & Nice ceded to France 1860; became Kingdom of Italy 1861.

polities.name: Kingdom of Sardinia (island)
polities.note: Viceroyalty under Aragon/Spain; Arborea held most of the island until 1420 (see Judicate of Arborea). British-held briefly 1708; Spanish reconquest 1717–1720; to Savoy 1720.

polities.name: Judicate of Arborea
polities.note: Last native Sardinian kingdom; c.1400 controlled most of the island except Cagliari and Alghero; defeated at Sanluri 1409; rights sold to Aragon 1420.

polities.name: Marquisate of Saluzzo

overlord.name: Kingdom of France (vassal, contested by Savoy)

polities.note: Del Vasto marquises; annexed by France 1548 (French until 1588, occupied by Savoy 1588, ceded to Savoy by Treaty of Lyon 1601).

polities.name: Marquisate of Montferrat
polities.note: Palaiologos marquises to 1533; Gonzaga of Mantua from 1536 (duchy 1574). Two non-contiguous parts (Upper/Lower Montferrat). Trino and Alba to Savoy 1631; rest to Savoy 1708.

polities.name: Duchy of Milan
polities.note: Visconti (to 1447) — Giangaleazzo's 1402 empire reached Bologna, Pisa, Siena and Perugia; Ambrosian Republic 1447–50; Sforza 1450–1499 and 1512–1515/1521–1535 (often held Genoa 1421–35, 1464–78, 1487–99). Lost Brescia/Bergamo to Venice 1426–28, Ticino to Swiss 1512, Parma–Piacenza 1512/1545. Spanish 1535–1706, Austrian 1706/1714–1796 (Mantua joined 1708; Novara, Tortona, Vigevano to Savoy 1738/48). Cisalpine Republic 1797.

polities.name: Republic of Venice
polities.note: Extent = Italian Terraferma only: Treviso, Vicenza/Verona 1404–05, Padua 1405, Friuli 1420, Brescia 1426, Bergamo 1428, Crema 1449, Rovigo/Polesine 1484; briefly Cremona and Romagna ports c.1499–1509. Stato da Mar (Istria, Dalmatia, Ionian islands, Crete to 1669, Cyprus 1489–1571, Morea 1699–1718) belongs to the Balkan/Mediterranean gazetteers. Partitioned 1797 (Campo Formio).

polities.name: Duchy of Mantua
polities.note: Gonzaga lordship 1328, marquisate 1433, duchy 1530; also ruled Montferrat from 1536. War of the Mantuan Succession 1628–31 (Gonzaga-Nevers). Annexed by Austria 1708.

polities.name: Duchy of Guastalla
polities.note: Torelli county 1406–1539, Gonzaga 1539 (duchy 1621); to Parma 1748.

polities.name: Duchy of Mirandola
polities.note: Pico family lordship/county (with Concordia), duchy 1619; sold to Modena 1711.

polities.name: Este dominions (Ferrara, Modena and Reggio)
polities.note: Este marquises of Ferrara; Modena and Reggio imperial duchy 1452, Ferrara papal duchy 1471. Ferrara devolved to the Pope 1598 and the court moved to Modena. Mirandola 1711; Massa-Carrara by inheritance 1829. Cispadane/Cisalpine 1796–1814.

polities.name: Duchy of Parma and Piacenza
polities.note: Created by Pope Paul III for the Farnese (Piacenza Spanish-occupied 1547–1585). Bourbon-Parma 1748 (with Guastalla). French 1802–1814. Before 1545 Parma and Piacenza were Milanese (to 1512) then Papal (1512–1545).

polities.name: Duchy of Massa and Carrara
polities.note: Malaspina marquisate, Cybo-Malaspina; principality 1568, duchy 1664; inherited by Modena 1829.

polities.name: Republic of Genoa
polities.note: Ligurian coast (both Rivieras). Also ruled Corsica (to 1768; rebel Corsican Republic from 1755). Andrea Doria's 1528 constitution and Spanish alignment. Finale purchased 1713. Ligurian Republic 1797.

polities.name: Corsican Republic
polities.note: Pasquale Paoli's republic in the interior; coastal towns stayed Genoese. Genoa ceded Corsica to France 1768; conquered 1769. (Kingdom of Corsica under Theodore 1736 brief.) Before 1755 Corsica was Genoese.

polities.name: Marquisate of Finale
polities.note: Del Carretto marquises to 1602; Spanish 1602–1713 (Milan's sea outlet); sold to Genoa 1713.

polities.name: Monaco
polities.note: Grimaldi lordship (princes from 1612); Menton and Roquebrune held until they seceded 1848 (sold to France 1861).

polities.name: Republic of Florence
polities.note: Medici-dominated from 1434; Pisa conquered 1406 (revolted 1494–1509), Livorno bought 1421, Cortona 1411. Republic restored 1494–1512 and 1527–30. Became Duchy of Florence 1532.

polities.name: Grand Duchy of Tuscany
polities.note: Duchy of Florence 1532, Siena 1557, Grand Duchy 1569. Medici to 1737, then Habsburg-Lorraine. Presidi and Piombino excluded. Kingdom of Etruria 1801–07; French departments 1807–14. Annexed to Sardinia/Italy 1859–60.

polities.name: Republic of Siena
polities.note: Southern Tuscany incl. Grosseto and the Maremma; besieged and taken by Florence/Spain 1555; Republic of Siena in Montalcino to 1559; Siena to Florence 1557.

polities.name: State of the Presidi
polities.note: Coastal fortresses (Orbetello, Porto Ercole, Porto Santo Stefano, Talamone, Ansedonia; Porto Longone on Elba); to Etruria 1801.

polities.name: Republic of Lucca
polities.note: Oligarchic republic (Guinigi signoria 1400–1430). Became Principality of Lucca and Piombino 1805, Duchy of Lucca 1815–1847 (Bourbon-Parma), then Tuscany.

polities.name: Principality of Lucca and Piombino
polities.note: Plus the Piombino exclave; Elisa also Grand Duchess of Tuscany 1809.

polities.name: Duchy of Lucca
polities.note: Bourbon-Parma holding pending return of Parma; merged into Tuscany 1847.

polities.name: Principality of Piombino
polities.note: Appiani lords (princes 1594) with Elba (except Portoferraio, Florentine 1548, and Porto Longone, Spanish); Ludovisi 1634, Boncompagni-Ludovisi 1701; French 1801; to Lucca and Piombino 1805.

polities.name: Duchy of Castro
polities.note: Farnese fief in northern Lazio; razed by papal troops 1649 (Wars of Castro).

polities.name: Papal States
polities.note: Before 1500 papal authority in Romagna, Marche and Umbria was nominal: signorie listed separately (Bentivoglio, Malatesta, Ordelaffi, Manfredi, Varano, Montefeltro/Urbino, Baglioni). Cesare Borgia and Julius II recovered Romagna and Bologna 1500–1506. Ferrara 1598, Urbino 1631. Legations lost 1797 (Cispadane) and 1860; Rome 1870. Enclaves: Benevento, Pontecorvo; Avignon and Comtat (France).

polities.name: Duchy of Urbino
polities.note: Montefeltro counts, dukes from 1443/1474; della Rovere from 1508 (added Pesaro 1513, Senigallia). Devolved to the Papal States 1631.

polities.name: Bentivoglio signoria of Bologna
polities.note: Bologna under Bentivoglio dominance (intermittently 1401–02, 1443–1506; Sante and Giovanni II); Julius II retook the city 1506.

polities.name: Malatesta signoria of Rimini
polities.note: Malatesta held Rimini, Cesena, Fano (Sigismondo Pandolfo, d.1468); much lost 1463; Rimini taken by Cesare Borgia 1500, briefly Venetian 1503–09; final papal recovery 1528.

polities.name: Sforza lordship of Pesaro
polities.note: Sforza of Pesaro (Alessandro, Costanzo, Giovanni); taken by Cesare Borgia 1500–03; to Urbino 1513. Before 1445 Malatesta.

polities.name: Ordelaffi lordship of Forlì
polities.note: Ordelaffi to 1480, then Girolamo Riario and Caterina Sforza (Forlì and Imola) until Cesare Borgia's conquest 1499–1500.

polities.name: Manfredi lordship of Faenza
polities.note: Manfredi signoria (also Imola at times); taken by Cesare Borgia 1501.

polities.name: Varano lordship of Camerino
polities.note: Da Varano lords, dukes 1515; Borgia interlude 1502–03; devolved to the Papacy 1539/1545.

polities.name: Baglioni signoria of Perugia
polities.note: Baglioni family dominated Perugia de facto under nominal papal sovereignty; ended by Paul III's Salt War 1540.

polities.name: Republic of San Marino
polities.note: Enlarged 1463 with Fiorentino, Montegiardino, Serravalle, Faetano.

polities.name: Patria del Friuli
polities.note: Ecclesiastical state of the Patriarch of Aquileia (Friuli, Cadore); conquered by Venice 1420.

polities.name: County of Gorizia
polities.note: Meinhardin counts of Görz also held the Puster valley/East Tyrol (Lienz); extinct 1500, inherited by Maximilian I.

polities.name: Kingdom of Naples
polities.note: Angevin-Durazzo to 1435 (Ladislaus, Joanna II), Aragonese conquest 1442, Trastámara line to 1501; Spanish viceroyalty 1504–1707; Austrian 1707–1734; Bourbon 1734 (Charles, Ferdinand). Parthenopean Republic Jan–Jun 1799. Napoleonic kingdom 1806–15 (Bourbons on Sicily). Merged into the Two Sicilies 1816. Papal enclaves Benevento and Pontecorvo excluded.

polities.name: Kingdom of Sicily
polities.note: Island kingdom; Aragonese viceroyalty from 1409/1412. Bourbon court refuge 1799 and 1806–1815 under British protection. Merged into the Two Sicilies 1816.

polities.name: Kingdom of the Two Sicilies
polities.note: Union of Naples and Sicily (Sicily: same island polygon as Kingdom of Sicily; revolt 1848–49). Conquered by Garibaldi/Sardinia 1860–61.

polities.name: Cisalpine Republic
polities.note: Lombardy, Valtellina, Modena-Reggio, the Legations (Bologna, Ferrara, Romagna), Venetian Brescia/Bergamo. Austro-Russian occupation 1799–1800. Became Italian Republic 1802.

polities.name: Napoleonic Italy (Italian Republic / Kingdom of Italy)
polities.note: Gained Venetia 1806, Marche 1808, South Tyrol (Trentino/Bozen) 1810; Istria/Dalmatia to Illyrian Provinces 1809.

polities.name: Ligurian Republic
polities.note: Annexed by France 1805; to Sardinia 1815.

polities.name: Roman Republic (1798–1799)
polities.note: Also the short-lived Roman Republic of 1849 (Mazzini) on the Papal States' territory.

polities.name: Kingdom of Lombardy–Venetia
polities.note: Austrian crown land; Lombardy to Sardinia 1859; Venetia (with Mantua) to Italy 1866. Republic of San Marco in Venice 1848–49.

polities.name: Kingdom of Italy
polities.note: Coarse peninsular envelope; Sicily and Sardinia included in the state but not in the polygon. Papal Lazio (separate entry) excluded until 1870; Venetia from 1866.

gaps.area: Upper Swabia (between Danube, Lech and Lake Constance)
gaps.note: Not empty: a mosaic of imperial abbeys (Kempten, Weingarten, Ochsenhausen, Salem), Waldburg and Königsegg counties, Further-Austrian Burgau/Nellenburg pieces, and small imperial cities (Memmingen, Kempten, Biberach, Ravensburg, Lindau). Not itemised; Further Austria, Augsburg bishopric, Ulm and Württemberg cover the edges.

gaps.area: Franconian/Swabian imperial knights' lands (Odenwald, Rhön, Spessart, Kraichgau)
gaps.note: Hundreds of tiny Reichsritter estates with no single ruler; also counties of Wertheim, Löwenstein, Erbach, Castell, Schwarzenberg. Fill with the surrounding prince-bishoprics (Würzburg, Bamberg, Mainz) or leave as fragmented.

Solms, Isenburg, Wied, Sayn, Leiningen, Manderscheid, Arenberg, Blankenheim, Virneburg, Sponheim (condominium of Baden and Palatinate) are not itemised. Imperial abbeys Stavelot-Malmedy and Prüm also omitted.

gaps.area: Lunigiana and the Langhe (Apennine imperial fiefs)
gaps.note: Malaspina marquisates of Lunigiana and Del Carretto/other imperial fiefs in the Langhe between Genoa, Montferrat and Piedmont; not itemised. Also small Po-valley fiefs (Correggio, Novellara, Sabbioneta, Bozzolo, Castiglione) under Gonzaga cadets.

gaps.area: Northern Westphalia and Lower Saxony minor lordships
gaps.note: Counties of Hoya and Diepholz (to Brunswick-Lüneburg 1582/1585), Rietberg, Spiegelberg, Pyrmont, Blankenburg, Regenstein, Hohnstein, Gleichen; imperial abbeys Corvey, Quedlinburg, Gandersheim, Essen, Werden — not itemised.
Individual cantons (Bern, Zurich, etc.), the common bailiwicks, Biel, Gersau and Engelberg are subsumed in the Old Swiss Confederacy entry.

Short-lived lordships after Giangaleazzo Visconti's death (1402) — Carrara of Padua (to 1405), Scaligeri remnants, Ordelaffi/Alidosi/Chiavelli/Trinci/Brancaleoni of Romagna, Marche and Umbria, Fondi/Orsini/Colonna baronies in Lazio — are only partly covered (the main Romagna/Marche ones are listed).
